ac.description: Two PWR-C49E-300AC-R supplies and the WS-X4993 fan tray - the switch as it runs, with every port empty

description: 48x 10/100/1000 RJ-45 and 4x 1/10G SFP+ 1RU top-of-rack switch running Cisco IOS, the front-to-back build of the Catalyst 4948E. All fifty-two ports, the console and management jacks, the status lamps and the recessed reset switch are on the front; two 300 W supplies and one four-fan tray between them are on the rear. Ports number 1-52 and run DOWN each column - odd on the top row, even beneath it. Its back-to-front sibling, the WS-C4948E-F, takes different supplies and a different fan tray and is not this device. End-of-sale was announced in October 2016.

gaps.wanted: A flat drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. The guide's Figures 1-1 and 1-2 show the lid and one side isometrically - a logo and labels on the lid, bracket screw holes and small slots on the side - and the data sheet says the chassis has "no side or top venting". None can be measured. Each of the four carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked.

What is printed above each column of jacks and above the two SFP+ columns. The data sheet's front photograph shows a short legend over every column, about 2 mm tall, and at 1.86 px per mm it is a grey smudge. The numerals under the lamps resolve as digits in the same photograph, which is the control: printing of that size is at the image's limit, so this is unresolved and not blank. A front photograph at 5 px per mm settles it.

A face for the 300 W DC-input supply, PWR-C49-300DC. The guide's Figure A-12 draws it isometrically with its terminal block and the data sheet lists it; no flat image of it is held, so the bays accept only the AC supply here.

A mechanical drawing or a photograph at several pixels per millimetre. Every position on both faces is read at under 2 px per mm. The repeating features are pinned by the registry; the lamps, the legends and the reset switch are each good to about half a millimetre.
The fan tray's draw. Neither document gives a figure for WS-X4993 apart from the switch.

attrs.redundancy-note: One tray of four fans. The data sheet says the tray has "redundant fans" and the guide that the remaining fans speed up to compensate for one that fails; neither gives an N+1 form, so none is written here.

mgmt.mixed: the out-of-band pair at the right of the front - an RJ-45 console port over a 10/100/1000 RJ-45 Ethernet management port - and the recessed reset switch beside the status lamp. Two jobs, one purpose: reaching and restarting the switch when the data plane cannot.

attrs.redundancy-note: Data sheet Table 1, "Power redundancy: 1+1 AC or DC", and the guide's Figure 1-2, which names the two bays power supply 1 (primary) and power supply 2 (redundant).

name: ws-c4948e

colour.note: The front face is the median of 2400 pixels of bare plate under the third block in the data sheet's Figure 1, #d3d4d1. The lamp strips are a pale yellow there; their value and the ink's are chosen by eye against the same photograph.

console-over-management.note: Figure 1-1 points callout 5, the console port, at the upper jack of the stacked pair and callout 3, the management port, at the lower; Figure 1-7 puts the MGT lamp under the stack. The management jack takes the bare part because its lamp is that one on the bottom row, not a pair in the bezel.

gate-1.note: BOTH DATA-SHEET PHOTOGRAPHS PASS, AT LOW RESOLUTION. The front, Figure 1, is 907 x 217 px with the face 827 px across and 84 tall: 9.85 against the stated 444.4 / 44.45 = 10.0, 1.5% out. The rear, Figure 2, is 853 px by 84: 10.15, 1.5% the other way. Scaled on the stated width the front is 1.861 px per mm, AND THE RJ-45 PITCH THEN READS 13.97 mm - 26.0 px, averaged over the 20 steps inside the four blocks of one row - which is the 0.550 in ganged-jack pitch the registry's rj45-ganged notes record from a TE 2x6 magjack, on a quantity the scale never saw. The registry states that pitch in its notes and not as a key, so the block gives 13.97 as a number; the 12.7 part leaves 1.27 mm of wall between openings, as the photograph shows. The SFP+ pair steps 14.5 against the registry's 14.25. So both axes are read off the photographs, and at under 2 px per mm every position is good to about half a millimetre and no better.

interface-names.note: NOT IN EITHER STAGED CISCO DOCUMENT. Searched the installation guide and the data sheet for GigabitEthernet, FastEthernet and their short forms and found nothing; port naming lives in the IOS configuration guides, which are not staged. The names are the NetBox devicetype-library device type for this model, a community file (netbox-community/devicetype-library, device-types/Cisco/WS-C4948E.yaml): GigabitEthernet1/1 to 1/48, TenGigabitEthernet1/49 to 1/52 and FastEthernet1 for the management port. THAT FILE ALSO TYPES THE MANAGEMENT PORT 100BASE-TX, which its name suggests and Cisco's own documents contradict - the guide says "a 10/100/1000 RJ-45 port Ethernet Management port" and the data sheet "10/100/1000BASE-TX" - so the name is taken from it and the speed from Cisco. Estimated, because a community file is the only source for the names.

lamps.note: Installation guide, Table 1-5 and Table 1-1. STATUS: green up and running, red system fault, flashing amber power-on self-test. Port LINK lamps: green link, amber disabled, blinking amber link fault. FAN: green tray OK, red a fan has failed. PS1 and PS2: green input power OK, red fault. The management lamp is the data sheet's "green (good), orange (disabled), or off (not connected)". Positions are Figure 1-7's callouts placed on the photograph: PS1, PS2 and FAN in a column at the right, MGT and STATUS on the bottom row with the recessed RESET beside STATUS.

port-order.note: Each block prints twelve lamps in one row under its six columns, alternately an up and a down triangle, with a numeral under each running 1 to 12, 13 to 24 and so on. Two lamps per column, up then down, so the odd port is the upper jack. The four uplink lamps under the SFP+ cages run the same way with 49 to 52 beneath them, on a row of their own that reads about a millimetre higher than the jack lamps' (centred 36.0 mm down against 37.1). SO A NUMERAL SITS UNDER ITS LAMP AND NOT UNDER ITS JACK: twelve lamps on a 5.8 mm step stand beneath six columns on a 13.97 step, and L61 reports the sixteen numerals that land within a millimetre or so of their jack's centre by accident. The legends printed ABOVE the jacks are not legible at this resolution and are a gap.

power.note: Data sheet Table 2: "Typical operating power 230W at 25C" and "Maximum power 275W at 55C"; Table 1 calls the first "230W average". These are the switch's draw, ambient stated, configuration not. Heat is printed three ways and they are not one measure: the data sheet gives 1173 BTU per hour on AC input and 1251 on DC, and the guide's Table 1-2 gives 1364 BTU/hour "worst case". The guide's is carried, as the largest.

rear-face.note: The data sheet's Figure 2 at 1.919 px per mm. Supply 1 runs 8 to 230 px, the fan tray 232 to 598, supply 2 from 600 to 822, and a strip of bare chassis with an earth mark closes the face. The guide's Figure 1-2 names them in the same order: power supply 1 (primary), fan tray, power supply 2 (redundant).

rows.note: Jack openings read 69-86 and 97-114 px down a face that runs from 53 to 137, 84 px for the stated 44.45 mm, so at 0.529 mm per px the rows centre 12.9 and 27.7 mm down: tops at 7.4 and 22.2 for an 11.0 part, a 14.8 step. The upper jacks show their keyways up and the lower their keyways down, the usual stacked mirror. The SFP+ openings centre 12.5 and 27.5, which is the registry's 15.0 belly-to-belly step, upper cage upright over the lower turned 180.

sources.note: Four sources, none of them committed. (1) Catalyst 4948E and Catalyst 4948E-F Switch Installation Guide, OL-21561-02, 162 pages: Table 1-1 features, Table 1-2 specifications, Figures 1-1, 1-2 and 1-7, Table 1-5 LEDs, appendix A power supplies. (2) Cisco Catalyst 4948E and 4948E-F Ethernet Switches Data Sheet, c78-598933, 9 pages: Table 1, Table 2, Table 4, and Figures 1 to 3, which are square-on photographs of the front and of both rear builds. (3) Cisco's end-of-sale notice EOL11273. (4) Photographs of real units from resale listings, for what the small data-sheet photographs cannot resolve. THE GUIDE'S OWN CHASSIS FIGURES ARE ISOMETRIC LINE DRAWINGS and gave callouts only. No vendor 3D model and no stencil render was found.

the-four-blocks.note: The 24 columns stand in four blocks of six. Their first openings read 25, 193, 361 and 531 px - steps of 168, 168 and 170 - so a least-squares block step of 90.59 mm starting at 10.4, a 6.77 gutter. That fits the four starts to 0.2, 0.1, 0.7 and 0.3 mm. A captive-looking screw sits in each gutter and a fourth before the uplinks.

the-width.note: 17.5 in is 444.5 mm; both documents print "1.75 x 17.5 x 19.4 in. (4.4 x 44.4 x 49.3 cm)". 444.4 x 44.45 x 492.8 is carried: the metric width as printed, and the inch figures converted for height and depth, which the metric rounds to a millimetre. The photographs show no ears, and the RJ-45 pitch closing on the registry at that width says the figure is the body. The rack-mount brackets are a separate kit.
